column3: Self-nomination or nomination by another person is permitted. Use a simple, accessible nomination; polished writing, status, money or popularity must not create advantage.
column7: Relevant Subject-Matter Reviewer A
column8: Must understand the award's actual discipline or purpose.

column3: Verify award-specific eligibility and evaluation-period requirements before scoring. Ineligible nominees do not receive a score.
column7: Relevant Subject-Matter Reviewer B
column8: Provides a second independent domain perspective.

column3: Each Selection Circle member discloses conflicts before seeing/scoring the full nominee file when reasonably possible; conflicted members recuse.
column7: AMW Steward Reviewer
column8: Understands AMW architecture, dignity, Stewardship and award controls; should not be in a conflicted direct line to nominee.

column3: Review proportionate evidence tied to the award's meaning. Evidence may include work product, observation, results, demonstration, records, or voluntary statements; no unnecessary private information.
column7: Legacy / Community Representative
column8: Represents the people/community/Legacy context affected by the award.

column3: All five voting reviewers score independently using the Universal Scoring Rule before group discussion.
column7: Rotating Independent Reviewer
column8: Adds independence and reduces institutional familiarity bias.

column3: The Circle reviews final independent scores, evidence sufficiency and material score variance. Calibration corrects misunderstanding; it does not force consensus or engineer a winner.
column7: Selection Records Steward
column8: Maintains process, evidence list, score calculations, recusals and record; does not vote.

column3: Verify material facts, attribution/credit, eligibility, unresolved safety/welfare concerns where applicable, and calculation accuracy before selection becomes final.
The selected honoree chooses whether to accept recognition. Publicity, photograph, testimonial, biography and story-sharing are separate choices.
Recognize the honoree in the manner authorized. Declining publicity does not reduce the award or the honoree's standing.
Preserve the decision record, scoring, recusals, consent choice and learning. Return appropriate learning to the award system without turning nominees into permanent records of failure.

column7: Controlled Rule

column2: 100 points for scored awards; 100% verified participant choice for PC-01 awards
column3: Every scored award has five weighted criteria totaling 100. Founder-designated Participant Choice awards use PC-01 instead of panel scoring; their result is determined by verified participant ballots after eligibility/welfare screening.
column7: No public popularity voting, likes/followers, donor status, purchase, payment, title, tenure, visibility or personal closeness may create selection advantage.

column2: 0–5 for scored awards; not used for PC-01
column3: 0 = no qualifying evidence; 1 = minimal; 2 = emerging; 3 = meets; 4 = strong; 5 = exceptional. Participant Choice ballots are not converted into reviewer ratings.
column7: Family, close personal, financial, supervisory, mentoring or other material conflicts must be disclosed; conflicted reviewers do not score that nominee. A recused voting seat is replaced by another qualified reviewer so the final decision still uses five eligible independent votes.

column2: Rating ÷ 5 × criterion weight for scored awards
column3: Each reviewer produces one 0–100 weighted score. PC-01 awards use verified ballot counts rather than reviewer-weighted points.
column7: Collect only information reasonably necessary to determine eligibility and score award criteria.

column2: Average of five final reviewer scores for scored awards
column3: Do not discard a high or low reviewer score because it is inconvenient. PC-01 result = horse/candidate with the highest verified valid ballot count.
column7: Trauma, poverty, diagnosis, treatment history, criminal history, housing history or other hardship is never scored for severity to make someone more deserving.

column2: 80.0 / 100 for scored awards; no numeric threshold for PC-01
column3: A scored award may have no recipient below 80. A PC-01 award may have no recipient when no eligible candidate exists, welfare/integrity gates fail, or the ballot cannot responsibly be verified.
column7: Nomination, program participation, services, resources and award receipt do not create consent for photographs, testimonial, biography, public story or stage appearance.

column2: 15 points between highest/lowest reviewer total for scored awards
column3: Triggers calibration for scored awards. PC-01 uses ballot-integrity review rather than reviewer-score variance.
column7: Child nominees are evaluated developmentally and relative to opportunity/effort; no adult achievement standard, unnecessary sensitive questioning or publicity without required guardian/child permissions.

column2: Scored awards: highest-weighted criterion → Stewardship/Safety/Dignity → evidence quality → predetermined neutral method; PC-01: equal top ballot counts → predetermined neutral method
column3: No popularity manipulation or subjective last-minute preference may break a tie.
column7: Technical, food, animal and care awards require responsible safety/welfare practice. Verified serious reckless disregard may make a nominee ineligible for that cycle; ordinary learning mistakes are not automatically punitive.

column2: One decimal place for scored-award final average; whole verified ballot counts for PC-01
column3: Keep reviewer calculations unrounded for scored awards. Preserve exact ballot counts for Participant Choice awards.
column7: Accept multiple reasonable evidence forms. Expensive portfolios, polished applications or professional networks cannot become hidden eligibility requirements.
Reviewers score independently before deliberation; group influence cannot substitute for evidence.

column1: SELECTION CIRCLE ADAPTATIONS — same five-vote structure, different required expertise
column7: The Legacy never gives an award merely because the award exists.

column3: Standard five-seat Circle.
column7: Materially equivalent nominees are resolved only through the published tie rule and predetermined neutral method.

column3: At least one subject-matter seat includes youth-development/safeguarding knowledge; child is never judged by adult access/status standards.
column7: A nominee may raise a conflict/process concern. Review asks whether the process was followed; it is not retaliation and does not guarantee a different outcome.

column3: At least one subject-matter seat has credible discipline-specific technical competence; applicable safety gate is verified.
column7: Credit follows the person/people who actually created, performed, built, cared for, discovered or contributed the work.

column3: At least one subject-matter seat understands the relevant creative/technical field; popularity metrics are excluded as selection drivers.
column7: Nominee files and detailed scoring are limited to people with a legitimate selection/governance reason to access them.

column3: At least one subject-matter seat has dog/animal welfare, training, husbandry or aquatic-care competence as applicable.
column7: When a Founder-designated Participant Choice award is used, each eligible participant receives one equal private ballot, may abstain, and is not required to explain the choice. Staff, handlers, family members, donors or other adults may not direct, purchase, pressure, campaign for or manufacture a participant's vote.

column3: At least one subject-matter seat has appropriate program/safeguarding knowledge; sensitive identity/health/recovery facts are not required merely to prove worthiness.

Same five-vote structure; at least one canine behavior/welfare reviewer and one humane training/handling reviewer as applicable. Barclay's voluntary behavior is evidence and may not be manufactured through force, staged competition, monopolized access or inducement during selection observations.

Selection Circle does not choose the favorite. It verifies candidate eligibility, animal welfare, participant eligibility, one-person/one-ballot integrity, neutral counting and the tie rule. At least one animal-welfare/husbandry reviewer and one independent ballot verifier are required.
